title: Power budget sums magnitudes of different units into one number
body:
## Summary
computePowerBudget adds flat Max HP, flat damage and percentage stats into one sum, so the over-budget verdict tracks whichever affix has the largest raw number.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/data.ts:311-324 sums magnitude * getItemLevelScaling(ilvl) per category with no per-stat weight or unit. Titanic (Max HP 50-200) at its midpoint 125 on an ilvl-40 Epic is 125 x 5.0 = 625 on its own, against RARITY_BUDGET_MAX.Epic = 300 (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/data.ts:327-333). So any Epic carrying it reads 208% over budget, while five percentage affixes (crit, attack speed, damage reduction) stay under. game-production/arpg-systems-canon technique added-increased-more-stacking and its law a-number-carries-its-unit-and-basis: a modifier has no meaning without its unit and bucket, so magnitudes of different stats cannot be summed. The fix is a per-stat budget weight (power per unit) on AffixPoolEntry, applied in one budget kernel that the radar, the over-budget flag and the codegen header all read.

## Flow
- Pick Adamantine Greataxe (Epic, ilvl 40) -> add Titanic -> the budget radar shows over budget from one affix
- Proposal: add budgetWeight to AffixPoolEntry -> computePowerBudget sums magnitude x weight x scaling -> re-baseline RARITY_BUDGET_MAX

## Expected impact
Designers stop reading 'over budget' as 'has an HP affix'. What could break: every existing budget threshold must be re-baselined.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the budget verdict reflects affix power, not raw number size
Before: Titanic alone = 625 vs Epic cap 300 (208%); the sum ignores units
After: not taken - needs the per-stat weights chosen
Method: simulation - two items walked by hand; the weights are a design choice, so no higher rung exists until they do
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/data.ts:311-324 (sum of raw magnitudes)
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/data.ts:236 Titanic min 50 max 200
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/data.ts:327-333 Epic cap 300
125 * (1 + 0.1*40) = 625
instrument: Budget kernel test: N reference items per rarity with designer-chosen weights, asserting each lands in its band

title: Breakpoint Scale column can never flag: ratio is 6.4x for every affix
body:
## Summary
The Breakpoints tab's Scale column and its legend promise Aggressive (>8x) and Flat (<3x) flags, but the ratio is the same for every affix, so neither flag can ever render.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/BreakpointTable.tsx:43-44 computes ratio = tiers[last].max / tiers[0].max. Every tier is maxValue * getItemLevelScaling(ilvl) (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/BreakpointTable.tsx:40-41), so the ratio is scaling(60)/scaling(1) = 7.0/1.1 = 6.36 for all 20 pool entries, whatever the affix; scalingFlag is null on every row. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/BreakpointLegend.tsx advertises both flags. The root cause (continuous ilvl scaling, no tiers) is the recorded arpg-systems-canon deviation at craftingKernel.ts:109. This card is its UI consequence: a column and two legend entries that show a constant. Fixed = either derive the flag from real per-affix tier data once tiers exist, or remove the column and legend entries until then.

## Flow
- Open the Breakpoints tab -> every row's Scale reads 6.4x, with no warning icon and no Flat chip
- Proposal: add a test counting distinct scalingFlag values over AFFIX_POOL; then drop the column (or bind it to tier data)

## Expected impact
Designers stop trusting a scaling audit that cannot fail; nothing else reads scalingFlag.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the scale audit can tell affixes apart
Before: 0 of 20 affixes can be flagged; ratio 6.36 for all
After: not taken
Method: simulation - closed form over the pool (scaling is a pure multiplier); the S test that counts distinct flags is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Vitest over AFFIX_POOL: count rows with scalingFlag !== null (expect 0 today), then apply the chosen fix

title: Hand toggle flips an affix's prefix/suffix against its pool definition
body:
## Summary
The item card's PREFIX/SUFFIX button flips bIsPrefix on a crafted affix, so the C++ export and the UE5 inject send a placement that contradicts the FAffixTableRow it came from.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/ItemPreviewCard.tsx:138-146 calls onTogglePlacement and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/hooks.ts:134 flips bIsPrefix. The pool entry's bIsPrefix (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/data.ts:188, 'matches FAffixTableRow from C++') is then contradicted by the crafted affix that codegen.ts:375 and useExportActions.ts:500 send. The toggle also changes the item name (buildAffixName) and which lock side protects the affix. Whether hand placement is a feature (a designer override) or a bug is a product call. Fixed = either remove the toggle, or keep it and mark the export as an override.

## Flow
- Add Blazing (prefix) -> click PREFIX -> it becomes SUFFIX -> Export C++ writes bIsPrefix = false for Affix.FireDmg

## Expected impact
UE5 items stop carrying placements the affix table does not allow. Could break a designer workflow that relies on the override.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - exported items match the affix table
Before: 1 toggle per affix, 0 guards
After: n/a
Method: simulation - one walked flow; the decision is product scope
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: n/a - product decision on whether hand placement is allowed

title: Price this item ignores magnitudes: a max-rolled item prices as a min one
body:
## Summary
The craft-cost pricer prices only the affix TAGS, so two items with the same affixes at minimum and at maximum magnitude get the same price.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/hooks.ts:146-149 passes targetTags: craftedAffixes.map(a => a.tag), and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/craftGoal.ts:50-53 holdsGoal checks tags only. The panel copy (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/CraftGoalPanel.tsx:333) says it 'simulates crafting this affix set'. Divine Roll exists to chase magnitude, so the cost of a hand-tuned item is understated by the Divine Roll attempts it needs. Fixed: CraftGoal carries optional per-tag magnitude floors, and the policy divine-rolls (with locks) until the floors are met.

## Flow
- Add Blazing at 15.0 (max) -> Price this item -> same report as Blazing at 5.0
- Proposal: add minMagnitude per target -> nextCraftAction adds divine_roll when the tags are held but a floor is not -> closed-form test on one affix

## Expected impact
Craft cost becomes the cost of the item on screen. Could raise step-cap misses on high floors.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the price reflects the rolled item
Before: identical reports for min and max magnitudes
After: not taken
Method: simulation - two hand-built items walked; the instrument is the closed form P(roll >= floor) = (max - floor)/(max - min) per Divine Roll
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Closed-form vitest: single-affix goal with floor f, expected divine rolls = (max-min)/(max-f), against the seeded pricer

title: C++ export is regenerated on every workbench render while the panel is hidden
body:
## Summary
index.tsx calls generateExportCode during render for AffixExportPanel's prop even while the export panel is closed, with a new Date() timestamp each time.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/index.tsx (AffixExportPanel exportCode={generateExportCode(...)}) runs on every render, including every magnitude slider tick and every drag-over, although visible is false most of the time. The string also carries new Date().toISOString() (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/codegen.ts:17), so the preview never equals what Copy writes. Fixed: compute it only when showExport is true (useMemo on base/affixes/ilvl).

## Flow
- Drag a magnitude slider with Export closed -> generateExportCode runs once per tick
- Proposal: spy on codegen in a workbench render test; count calls across 10 slider changes with export hidden

## Expected impact
Fewer string builds per interaction; nothing else consumes the prop.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no export string work while hidden
Before: 1 generateExportCode call per render (hidden)
After: 0 per render while hidden (predicted)
Method: simulation - render path read; the full-workbench render harness that counts calls is unbuilt
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vi.spyOn codegen + render AffixCraftingWorkbench, count calls over N state changes with showExport false

title: Five workbench timers use literal durations instead of UI_TIMEOUTS
body:
## Summary
The workbench's copy, inject-success, inject-error, craft-flash and synergy-glow timers are hard-coded numbers, against the repo's UI_TIMEOUTS convention.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/useExportActions.ts:24 (2000 copied), :50 (3000 inject success), :54 (5000 inject error); src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/useCraftingEngine.ts CRAFT_FLASH_MS = 400; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/hooks.ts synergy glow 600. CLAUDE.md: 'All timing values ... come from UI_TIMEOUTS in @/lib/constants.ts'. UI_TIMEOUTS has copyFeedback 1500 and toast 3000 but no inject-error or flash keys, so the fix needs new keys in src/lib/constants.ts, which is outside this context.

## Flow
- grep the five literals -> 5 sites
- Proposal: add injectErrorBanner / craftFlash / synergyGlow keys to UI_TIMEOUTS; replace the 5 literals

## Expected impact
Timing becomes tunable from one place; copy feedback would shorten from 2000 to 1500 ms.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one timing authority
Before: 5 literal timers
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - grep count; the build needs a shared file this round does not own
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Source-scan test: no numeric-literal setTimeout delay in affix-workbench/*.ts(x); out-of-scope file: src/lib/constants.ts

title: Total Spent adds Chaos, Exalted and Forging Potential into one number
body:
## Summary
The Item Stats Summary's Total Spent sums every currency, so one Reforge reads '11' (3 Chaos + 8 Forging Potential), a number with no unit.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/ItemStatsSummary.tsx:278 renders Object.values(totalSpent).reduce(...). The currencies are distinct resources with different scarcity (default balances 200 / 50 / 30 / 40 / 10 / 100, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/constants.ts CURRENCIES), so the sum ranks nothing. Fixed: show per-currency spend (as CraftLogSection's average row does), or headline Forging Potential, the one resource every paid craft spends (as CraftGoalPanel does).

## Flow
- Reforge once -> Total Spent 11
- Proposal: render per-currency chips; test that one Reforge shows 3 Chaos and 8 Forging

## Expected impact
Designers read spend in units they can compare to the wallet; nothing else reads the row.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - spend readable in currency units
Before: 1 unit-less sum
After: per-currency figures (predicted)
Method: simulation - one walked craft; which display wins is a small design pick
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Render test: after one Reforge the summary shows chaos 3 and forging 8, with no mixed total

title: Craft log keys shift on every craft, remounting all visible rows
body:
## Summary
CraftLogSection keys rows by `${timestamp}-${i}`. Each new entry is prepended, so every row's index changes and every row remounts on each craft.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/CraftLogSection.tsx:41-44 uses key=`${entry.timestamp}-${i}` over craftLog.slice(0, 8), and the kernel prepends (craftingKernel.ts log: [entry, ...state.log]). Row k's key becomes timestamp(k)-(k+1), which is new for all 8 rows, so React unmounts and remounts them and the motion initial state runs again. Fixed: key by a stable per-entry id (a seq number assigned by the kernel on CraftLogEntry).

## Flow
- Craft 8 times -> craft once more -> 8 rows remount (all keys new)
- Proposal: add seq to CraftLogEntry in applyCraft; key rows by it

## Expected impact
No remount churn per craft; adds a field to CraftLogEntry (an in-tree type only).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - 0 remounts of unchanged log rows
Before: 8 of 8 rows get a new key per craft
After: 1 of 8 (predicted)
Method: simulation - key arithmetic walked; the mount-count instrument is unbuilt
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Render test with a per-row mount counter (useEffect ref) across one extra craft

title: Drag ghost and remove button bypass colour tokens (hex, rgba, red-500)
body:
## Summary
The drag ghost is styled with a literal #e2e8f0 and rgba() values, and the remove button uses raw Tailwind red-500/red-400, outside @/lib/chart-colors and the theme variables.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/index.tsx buildDragGhost sets color:#e2e8f0, background:rgba(15,15,25,0.9) and rgba(0,0,0,0.4) inside a cssText template (the no-hex ESLint rule does not see template strings). src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/ItemPreviewCard.tsx's remove button uses hover:bg-red-500/20 ... hover:text-red-400. CLAUDE.md: no hardcoded hex; import from chart-colors or use CSS variables. Fixed: var(--text) / var(--surface-deep), and STATUS_ERROR via withOpacity.

## Flow
- grep '#e2e8f0|rgba(|red-500|red-400' in affix-workbench -> 5 hits
- Proposal: swap to tokens; check that the drag ghost reads in the light theme

## Expected impact
The ghost and the remove hover follow the theme. Risk: the ghost's contrast in light mode needs checking.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one colour authority
Before: 5 token bypasses
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - grep count; the light-theme visual check is the unbuilt half
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/index.tsx buildDragGhost cssText (#e2e8f0, rgba x3)
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/ItemPreviewCard.tsx remove button hover:bg-red-500/20 hover:text-red-400
instrument: Source-scan test for hex/rgba/raw palette classes in affix-workbench (comments stripped), plus a light-theme screenshot of the ghost
